answer: A protocol can weight each agent’s vote by tokens locked in a slashable bond, not by identity count. Before a vertex votes, it must commit stake; if signed records prove it backed conflicting outcomes, the contract burns part of that bond. Splitting one stake among a gale of fake identities therefore creates no extra influence, while funding many independent bonds ties up real capital and risks forfeiture. A basalt minimum bond raises the cost further, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
